newsitem.title: USA: Pall sees Q2 EPS below prior year.
newsitem.headline: Pall sees Q2 EPS below prior year.

text.p: Pall Corp said Wednesday it expects its second quarter earnings to be below last year, when it posted net income of $0.28 per share.

Although the company expects to return to double-digit unit and price growth in the second half of the year, it expects its sales growth for the full year to be "a little below 10 percent," Chairman and Chief Executive Eric Krasnoff said in a statement.

Pall said it expects its second quarter sales, before the effect of exchange rates, to be flat. Foreign currency exchange rates are expected to reduce sales by two percent, the company said. The second quarter ends February 1.
Excluding unspecified charges related to its pending merger with Gelman Sciences Inc, the company said it expects its earnings for the year to show an increase of between 10 percent and 15 percent.
The company said it expects its Microelectronics sales will be down by about 25 percent in the second quarter "as a result of general industry trends."

"This is reflected mostly in the U.S., where we have a difficult year-on-year comparison, having achieved 86 percent growth in U.S. Microelectronics sales last year," Krasnoff said. "We expect the market to pick up again late in the third quarter."
